I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so at the start of the season I would stay with the wheat-maize rotation that fits the local climate, irrigation conditions, and market reality. I would keep winter wheat on most of the land because it is the stable base of my income, and then follow it with summer maize because that double-cropping system uses the full year well. Since I am well educated, I would lean toward improved or hybrid seed, soil-test-style balanced fertilization, and tighter water and pest management instead of farming by habit alone. I would avoid spreading land across too many crops because that raises management complexity and market risk; I would rather run two main crops well than several crops badly. For wheat, I would use moderate nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium to support tillering, rooting, and grain filling, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use targeted. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed, somewhat higher nitrogen, and fewer irrigations if rainfall is decent, with weed and insect control timed to field pressure. I would use rotary tillage for most fields because it is practical and efficient in this rotation system, and I would aim for steady, high but realistic yields rather than chasing maximum input use.
